title: VRAM budget math: weights, activations, caches

questions.q: In the VRAM budget formula provided in the lesson, what is the value of the safety factor (S) used to account for fragmentation and overhead?
questions.why: The lesson explicitly states: 'In our lab, S = 1.2. This means we expect to use 20% more memory than the raw sum of weights, activations, and caches.'

questions.q: According to the lesson, what is the activation fraction (fa) used to estimate activation memory (A) relative to weight memory (W)?
questions.why: The text defines the activation memory formula as A = W × fa and states: 'In our lab, we set fa = 0.1 (10% of weight size).'

questions.q: Based on the lab results, why is a 12B model in BF16 precision considered too large for a 24GB GPU?
options: The weight memory alone exceeds the available VRAM.
The total estimated VRAM usage is approximately 30.85 GB, which exceeds the ~20GB available after reserve.
The safety factor is too high for BF16 models.
BF16 requires more memory than FP32.
questions.answer: The total estimated VRAM usage is approximately 30.85 GB, which exceeds the ~20GB available after reserve.
questions.why: The lesson states: 'RESULT 12B_bf16 = 3.312e+10: This is approximately 30.85 GB. It proves that even BF16 is too large for a 24GB card...'

questions.q: Which class in ComfyUI is described as the 'gatekeeper' that tracks which weights are on the GPU and which are offloaded to CPU?
questions.why: The lesson states: 'The ModelPatcher class in comfy/model_patcher.py is the gatekeeper. It tracks which weights are on the GPU and which are offloaded to CPU.'

questions.q: According to the 'Common mistakes' section, why might increasing the batch size break the VRAM budget even if the weights fit?
options: Because weights are loaded in higher precision.
Because activations depend on batch size and increase linearly.
Because the safety factor increases with batch size.
questions.answer: Because activations depend on batch size and increase linearly.
questions.why: The lesson lists 'Assuming Activations are Constant' as a mistake, noting: 'in practice, increasing batch size will increase A linearly, potentially breaking your budget even if weights fit.'
